‘F the Iranian Leadership’: Bessent Says Death Threats Prove Economic Campaign Working — Regime a ‘Cornered Animal’

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a defiant message to Iran's leadership Friday, declaring that death threats against him would not deter his efforts to economically isolate the regime but instead demonstrated that the Trump administration's campaign was working.
The post ‘F the Iranian Leadership’: Bessent Says Death Threats Prove Economic Campaign Working — Regime a ‘Cornered Animal’ appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a defiant message to Iran’s leadership Friday, declaring that death threats against him would not deter his efforts to economically isolate the regime but instead demonstrated that the Trump administration’s campaign was working.

Speaking on CNBC’s Squawk Box, Bessent confirmed that he had relocated to a military base following Iranian threats against his life, while vowing to press ahead with Operation Economic Outcast, the administration’s sweeping campaign to economically isolate Tehran.

“F the Iranian leadership,” Bessent declared, insisting that he and other Cabinet members would not be intimidated by the threats. “It means what we are doing with Operation Economic Outcast is working.”

Bessent questioned why he should fear Iranian threats when American military personnel stationed in the Persian Gulf and President Donald Trump himself routinely face similar dangers, portraying the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as increasingly desperate.

“What we’re doing is working,” he said, describing the IRGC as “like a dangerous cornered animal.”

The Treasury secretary said his relocation followed instructions from the Secret Service, which advised him to leave his private residence amid the threats.

His confirmation followed a report earlier this week that Iranian threats against Bessent had progressed beyond an advanced stage, prompting his relocation with his family to military housing, according to a senior administration official.

“Threats against Sec. Bessent reached more than an advanced stage, which is why he and his family made the move,” the official said, according to Fox News.

The threats have focused attention on Bessent’s central role in directing the administration’s economic offensive, which has sought to deprive Tehran of the revenue needed to sustain its military and terrorist proxies.

Bessent blasted The Wall Street Journal for publishing an aerial photograph of his Georgetown home in January 2025, accusing the newspaper of exposing his residence despite requests that the image be withheld for security reasons.

He called the decision “highly irresponsible and dangerous,” likening the newspaper’s news operation to the “TMZ of financial news.”

The threats come as Operation Economic Outcast, launched in late August, intensifies the administration’s efforts to cut off Tehran’s remaining financial lifelines, while the U.S. naval blockade continues to restrict Iranian oil...
